reports.name: Homarus gammarus
reports.shape: A continuous robust carapace, unequal naked crusher/cutter palms, shorter crusher fingers, a spiny rostrum without a ventral tooth, eight jointed walking limbs including small P2/P3 chelae, six overlapping abdominal plates and a five-part tail fan replace the oval/rod draft.
reports.surface: Selected dark blue cuticle, restrained cream speckles, reddish palms and antennae, pale seam edges and original curved surfaces remain on the same retained model through all actions.
reports.remaining: Exact body ratios, rostral teeth, orbital/buccal plates, cutting dentition, joint axes, telson/uropod struts and setal fields remain unmeasured or incomplete. Palms, dorsal grooves and pleurae are still simplified. First sex-modified pleopods are not reconstructed. The source photo does not establish sex, optics or the entire species' variation.

reports.name: Homarus americanus
reports.shape: A separately proportioned robust carapace, a ventral rostral tooth, one broader crusher and a longer-fingered cutter, eight supported articulated walking limbs with small P2/P3 claws, six serial abdominal plates and a central telson with four uropod lobes replace the generic draft.
reports.surface: A warm red/olive selected phenotype follows the authentic lit NOAA/NURP source image. Smooth naked palms, fine varied cuticle and pale seams replace the undifferentiated tan surface; no generated photograph or measured material map is used.
reports.remaining: Rostral tooth variability, fine cuticular detail, setal structures, mouthparts, joint axes, claw dentition and internal physiology remain incomplete/unmeasured. The red/olive selection does not represent all natural coloration, and the photograph cannot calibrate illumination or reflectance. Sex/age are not independently redetermined; modified first pleopods are omitted.

reports.name: Nephrops norvegicus
reports.shape: A slender ridged carapace, authored kidney-shaped eye ends, three lateral rostral spine pairs with a ventral tooth cue, unequal elongated ridged palms, four pairs of jointed walking limbs with small P2/P3 chelae, six sculptured abdominal plates and a separate five-part fan replace the generic lobster.
reports.surface: Dorsal orange and a lighter underside, longitudinal palm/carapace ridge cues, small spine rows and pale serial seam margins are original numerical cuticle surfaces. The selected captive photograph guides the orange/cream appearance without calibrating material properties.
reports.remaining: Fine eye contour, rostral variation, spine/denticle positions, setal density, scaphocerite shape, detailed grooves and joints remain approximate. The mild selected abdominal arch does not reproduce every captive/wild posture. First sex-modified pleopods and internal organs are incomplete; the source photo does not independently establish sex or stage.
